purpose: M14-PRE-ORAO: the exact ORAO VRF-with-callback program bytes that run on Solana devnet, for local LiteSVM compatibility checks. Read-only fetch; nothing was sent to any cluster.

elf.length_rule: ELF64-LE end = max(e_shoff + e_shnum*e_shentsize, max(p_offset+p_filesz over program headers), max(sh_offset+sh_size over non-NOBITS sections)); the three agree up to the section header table, which is the last thing in the file

packet_cross_check.explanation: The packet hashed the whole 616,464-byte post-header payload (ELF plus 4192 bytes of zero allocation padding); orao-devnet.so is the 612272-byte ELF only, so its own sha256 differs from the packet value while the payload hash is identical.  sha256(header || orao-devnet.so || zeros(padding)) reproduces account_data_sha256.

real: the NetworkState and treasury account snapshots in orao-devnet-accounts.json (read as fixtures only: decoded and compared, never installed as the active network state)
synthetic: the active NetworkState is created locally by the devnet binary's own initialize/configure under the harness payer, request_fee 300,000 and callback_deadline 9,000 slots copied from the real snapshot but with ONE synthetic fulfil authority ([0x55; 32] keypair) and a synthetic treasury
the four real fulfil authorities (2VYNr8yM..., A9iZdgYa..., 9ZTHWWZD..., HSCqQaDH...) cannot sign locally, so no real devnet oracle behaviour is exercised
the Squads program is the test-only stand-in unless a squads_devnet_compat test loads the real Squads binary
LiteSVM default rent schedule, not devnet rent

reproduce: curl -s https://api.devnet.solana.com -H 'content-type: application/json' -d '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"method":"getAccountInfo","params":["7mzfTTbQ4h7S9uNFdzbVUCs7srF6hiLa52y4eotkp1MD",{"encoding":"base64","commitment":"finalized"}]}'; base64-decode result.value.data[0]; drop the 45-byte header; keep elf_len bytes where elf_len is computed by the length_rule.
limits: A read-only snapshot of bytes: not a deployment, a liveness receipt, or evidence that the devnet oracle fulfils our requests.

recheck_unchanged.note: Same read-only getAccountInfo repeated about 6,600 slots after the first fetch (about 45 minutes): the account data hashes are identical, i.e. neither the ProgramData nor the NetworkState changed during the work.
